perl_cache: none: Ensembl VEP read its transcripts from chr21_genes.gtf.gz through --gtf (no --cache, no --offline, which would switch the cache on as well); vep-rs reads json_cache, built from the same file
fasta: GRCh38 chromosome 21 at its full length from Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.primary_assembly.fa, every base outside the regions a run reads (each cached transcript's span with 5,000 bases of flank and each record with 2,000) masked to N; reference.fa.gz beside this file, compressed with bgzip, with reference.fa.gz.fai and reference.fa.gz.gzi for the compressed file and reference.fa.fai for its decompressed form; Ensembl VEP received the decompressed file as --fasta on every run and vep-rs the compressed one
input: 74 records on chromosome 21 inside eight genes of the Ensembl 116 GTF (PWP2 and TMPRSS3, protein coding on either strand; LINC00308 and PLAC4, lncRNA; ANKRD30BP1, an unprocessed pseudogene; TMEM97P1, a processed pseudogene; RNU6-1149P, an snRNA; MIR6070, a miRNA): the ClinVar GRCh38 records inside their spans, chosen by vep-golden-corpus select for every consequence set Ensembl VEP's --gtf route produces over them, and 21 synthetic single-base, two-base, deletion and insertion records written from the reference sequence inside, upstream and downstream of the non-coding genes

transcript_source.chr21_genes.gtf.gz: the lines of the eight genes from Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz (every feature type the release carries for them, the five header lines kept), sorted by start and end, bgzip-compressed and indexed with tabix -p gff
transcript_source.json_cache: vep-cache-builder --release 116 --assembly GRCh38 --species homo_sapiens --gtf chr21_genes.gtf.gz --genome-fasta reference.fa.gz --output-dir json_cache: the same bytes as the build from the whole primary-assembly FASTA, since the masked bases lie outside every transcript's span

filter-biotype.vep_command: vep -i variants.vcf -o <out> --gtf {corpus}/chr21_genes.gtf.gz --species homo_sapiens --assembly GRCh38 --format vcf --buffer_size 5000 --fork 1 --fasta <reference> --no_stats --quiet --force_overwrite --symbol --biotype --canonical --mane --tsl --protein --protein_version --gene_version --transcript_version --transcript_filter biotype is protein_coding [--tab|--vcf|--json]

generator: chr21_genes.gtf.gz: the eight genes' lines of the Ensembl 116 GTF, bgzip and tabix; json_cache: vep-cache-builder --gtf chr21_genes.gtf.gz --genome-fasta reference.fa.gz (the build the manifest's runs read); the masked reference as described under fasta, cut by scripts/fixtures/cut_plugin_regions.py --reference over the cache's transcripts and the records; expected outputs: one Ensembl VEP 116.3 container run per format for the manifest's run and each flag set from the vep command recorded here, the corpus mounted read-only at /work/corpus as its working directory and the decompressed reference at /work/ref.fa, the transcripts read from the GTF through --gtf and no cache mounted (the manifest's perl_mode gtf: the harness sets the source's SOURCE column and header lines aside); manifest: tools/vep-golden-corpus select over the --gtf route's reference for the ClinVar records inside the eight genes and the synthetic records, --include for every synthetic record and one PLAC4 record, --k 2 --seed 1 --max-records 80 --cache json_cache, then flag-set --perl-mode gtf, then classify for the manifest's run and the flag set against the committed tree's binary
